name: SpaceRyde
all_locations: San Francisco, CA, USA; Toronto, ON, Canada
long_description:
SpaceRyde is building the future of space cargo transportation to facilitate and encourage necessary in-space developments, innovations and economy. SpaceRyde is the only sustainable mode of space transportation. Its innovative system utilizes a stratospheric balloon to bypass the atmosphere without emissions nor depositing black particles into the ozone layer and is the world’s first and only multi-functional rocket. After completing its initial mission, the vehicle will remain powered in orbit and joins its rocket network until assigned its next in-space mission, including tasks such as; refuelling, deep space missions, space junk removal and de-orbiting. 

SpaceRyde’s story began in 2018 with husband-wife founders Saharnaz Safari and Sohrab Haghighat and the dream of eliminating the barriers to innovation in space. The company is now a rapidly growing team of over 30 employees with a 25,000-square-foot rocket factory and state-of-the-art engine groundworks facility.
one_liner: The Rocket Network: Sustainable & On-Demand Delivery Anywhere in Space

name: Velontra
long_description:
Velontra is building a hypersonic space plane that can takeoff from anywhere in any weather.  This horizontal takeoff increases launch reliability and enables customers to directly access any orbit.  Our air-breathing propulsion system is up to 6 times more fuel efficient than any rocket, and uses oxygen from the air which creates thousands of pounds of additional payload capacity. 

We have millions in current government/commercial contracts and LOI’s. 

We have assembled a team of industry experts, government senior executives, and a NASA astronaut. 

The hypersonic space plane will work by taking off from any runway with a jet propulsion system.  Next, it will climb to over 100,000’ and Mach 5.  At this point, it will launch a 2nd stage rocket directly into the desired Low Earth Orbit. 

Velontra is “boldly going where no one has gone before.”

launches.title: ✈️ Velontra - Hypersonic space plane that can take-off from any location and weather
launches.body:
Velontra is building a hypersonic space plane that can takeoff from anywhere in any weather.

Check us out at <https://velontra.com/>

**Problem**

1\.     Conventional Rocket-based launch is expensive (>$5000 per kg)

2\.     Rocket launch cancellations cost satellite companies millions

3\.     Launch lead times are greater than 1 year

4\.     Satellite companies do not get launched into their desired orbits

**Solution**

Velontra is building a hypersonic space plane that can takeoff from anywhere in any weather.  This horizontal takeoff increases launch reliability and enables customers to directly access any orbit.  Our air-breathing propulsion system is up to 6 times more fuel efficient than any rocket, and uses oxygen from the air which creates thousands of pounds of additional payload capacity.

![uploaded image](/media/?type=post&id=65001&key=user_uploads/848374/3cac1349-a095-4ac8-b60c-2753b8220b70)

**Revenue Generating Products**

Here are the steps of our tech development path.

1\.     Propulsion System

2\.     Supersonic UAV

3\.     Hypersonic UAV

4\.     Space Plane for Low Earth Orbit

**How It Works**

The hypersonic space plane will work by taking off from any runway with a jet propulsion system.  Next, it will climb to over 100,000’ and Mach 5.  At this point, it will launch a 2nd stage rocket directly into the desired Low Earth Orbit.

**Ask**

Our Ask is for introductions to any company putting anything into orbit.  We are pursuing LOI’s and customer discovery.

launches.title: RATLOG: Reusable heavy-lift rockets powered by an engine with 90% fewer parts
launches.tagline: First engine hot-fired in 4 months for under $30K. $400M in launch reservations signed.
launches.body:
𝗧𝗟;𝗗𝗥: Launch capacity is becoming a bottleneck, so we at RATLOG are 𝘁𝗮𝗸𝗶𝗻𝗴 𝗼𝗻 𝗦𝗽𝗮𝗰𝗲𝗫 with reusable heavy-lift rockets powered by an engine designed to use 𝟵𝟬% 𝗳𝗲𝘄𝗲𝗿 𝗽𝗮𝗿𝘁𝘀 than conventional designs. We built and successfully hot-fired our first engine in 𝗷𝘂𝘀𝘁 𝗳𝗼𝘂𝗿 𝗺𝗼𝗻𝘁𝗵𝘀 and have signed reservation agreements worth $𝟰𝟬𝟬𝗠. Now we are printing an engine with 𝟮𝟬𝟬𝘅 𝘁𝗵𝗲 𝘁𝗵𝗿𝘂𝘀𝘁 for a hot fire in November. If you’re a satellite operator, [reach out to us asap](https://calendar.app.google/xPzyR7iHmEJ3Gt116)**.**

<https://youtu.be/i-RuldD2YHU>	

𝗣𝗿𝗼𝗯𝗹𝗲𝗺

Satellite operators need to put more mass into orbit than ever, but an available launch slot can be 𝟯–𝟰 𝘆𝗲𝗮𝗿𝘀 𝗮𝘄𝗮𝘆 and cost up to $𝟭𝟱,𝟬𝟬𝟬 𝗽𝗲𝗿 𝗸𝗶𝗹𝗼𝗴𝗿𝗮𝗺. Every delay pushes back the start of operations and revenue.

As satellite constellations grow and new projects like space stations and orbital data centers take shape, customers need more launch capacity and more options.

As one European launch broker put it: “𝗜𝘁’𝘀 𝗴𝗼𝗹𝗱 𝗿𝗶𝗴𝗵𝘁 𝗻𝗼𝘄 𝗶𝗳 𝘆𝗼𝘂 𝗵𝗮𝘃𝗲 𝗮 𝘀𝗹𝗼𝘁.”

𝗦𝗼𝗹𝘂𝘁𝗶𝗼𝗻

We’re building 𝗿𝗲𝘂𝘀𝗮𝗯𝗹𝗲 𝗵𝗲𝗮𝘃𝘆-𝗹𝗶𝗳𝘁 𝗿𝗼𝗰𝗸𝗲𝘁𝘀 𝘁𝗼 𝗰𝗮𝗿𝗿𝘆 𝗽𝗮𝘆𝗹𝗼𝗮𝗱𝘀 𝗼𝗳 𝘂𝗽 𝘁𝗼 𝟮𝟬 𝘁𝗼𝗻𝗻𝗲𝘀, powered by an engine architecture that aims to use 𝟵𝟬% 𝗳𝗲𝘄𝗲𝗿 𝗽𝗮𝗿𝘁𝘀 than conventional designs.

We’ve 𝗲𝗹𝗶𝗺𝗶𝗻𝗮𝘁𝗲𝗱 𝘁𝗵𝗲 𝘁𝘂𝗿𝗯𝗼𝗽𝘂𝗺𝗽 by using a different method to pressurize the propellants and developed a **new rocket engine cycle** around it.

This simpler architecture reduces manufacturing complexity and cost, while reusability spreads the cost of the hardware across multiple flights.

Think of it as a 𝗯𝘂𝘀 𝘁𝗼 𝘀𝗽𝗮𝗰𝗲: customers book capacity on a shared flight and pay by the kilogram.

**Team**

Charlie and Paul met through mutual interest in rotating detonation engines for cruise missiles and started a club, then met Felix and Matty.

![uploaded image](/media/?type=post&id=122077&key=user_uploads/3173499/08b61f2e-5027-4a5d-912e-96e7381e9cd3)

From left to right

* 𝗙𝗲𝗹𝗶𝘅 𝗞𝗲𝗹𝗺, Chief Avionics Officer: Developed PCB designs since the age of 16.
* 𝗖𝗵𝗮𝗿𝗹𝗶𝗲 𝗪𝗲𝗶𝘀𝗲, Chief Executive Officer: Previously worked on ESA's Argonaut Moon Lander and space telescope.
* 𝗠𝗮𝘁𝘁𝘆 𝗗𝗿𝗶𝗲𝘀𝗻𝗮𝗰𝗸, Chief Operating Officer: Founding team at Lio (YC S23, a16z), working closely with CEO and COO.
* 𝗣𝗮𝘂𝗹 𝗞𝘂𝗻𝗵𝗮𝗿𝘁, Chief Technology Officer: Designed rocket engine nozzles for ESA's Argonaut lunar lander.

**Traction**

* Signed reservation agreements worth $𝟰𝟬𝟬𝗠.
* Built and successfully hot-fired our first rocket engine in 𝗷𝘂𝘀𝘁 𝗳𝗼𝘂𝗿 𝗺𝗼𝗻𝘁𝗵𝘀.
* Spoken with 𝟳𝟬+ 𝗽𝗼𝘁𝗲𝗻𝘁𝗶𝗮𝗹 𝗹𝗮𝘂𝗻𝗰𝗵 𝗰𝘂𝘀𝘁𝗼𝗺𝗲𝗿𝘀.

**Ask**

* If you’re building satellites, space stations, or orbital data centers, we’d love to discuss your launch plans. Book a meeting [here](https://calendar.app.google/xPzyR7iHmEJ3Gt116) or reach us at [charlie.weise@ratlog.space](mailto:charlie.weise@ratlog.space).
